verdict.rationale: Microsoft Graph documents REST endpoints for OneDrive driveItems. Items can be addressed by ID or path, uploaded via a single PUT (up to 250 MB) or a resumable upload session, and searched or delta-tracked across a folder hierarchy. However, the pack has no documented endpoint for download, direct folder listing, move, or delete. The only mention of moving files describes a user-facing feature, not an API call. Missing for 10: documented download/content-GET endpoint, list-children endpoint, move (PATCH parentReference) endpoint, delete endpoint, independent hands-on corroboration of API file operations.

support.subject: As a developer, files move through a real API — upload, download, list, move, and delete over documented REST endpoints, not just a desktop client

citations.quote: with Microsoft Graph, you can use a single API to work with them
By the driveItem unique identifier using drive/items/{item-id} By file system path using /drive/root:/path/to/file
Provide the contents of a new file or update the contents of an existing file in a single API call. This method only supports files up to 250 MB in size.
An upload session allows your app to upload ranges of the file in sequential API requests. It also enables the transfer to resume if the connection is dropped during the upload.
Search the hierarchy of items for items matching a query. You can search within a folder hierarchy, a whole drive, or files shared with the current user.
Track changes in a driveItem and its children over time.
